subject: Energy
title: BTUs and Other Units
description: Learn BTUs and Other Units in one minute.

hook.text: The British Thermal Unit (BTU) is still used in the US for heating and cooling—one BTU heats a pound of water by 1°F.

buildup.text: One BTU equals about 1,055 joules. Air conditioners are rated in BTUs per hour to show their cooling capacity.

discovery.text: The oil industry uses barrels of oil equivalent (BOE)—one barrel holds about 6.1 billion joules of energy.

twist.text: Tons of TNT measure explosive energy—one ton of TNT equals 4.2 billion joules, used for bombs and asteroids alike.

climax.text: Electron-volts measure atomic-scale energy—one eV is the energy an electron gains crossing one volt of potential.

punchline.text: Same concept, different scales—joules unite them all.

quiz.question: What does one BTU represent?
options: Energy to heat a pound of water by 1°F
Energy to boil a gallon of water
